correctness.rationale: Matching graph is exactly (d+1)-regular. In the fan, the block-eigenvector equations yield the single resolvent root λ-d=nR_v(λ), uniquely above d. Star containment and a bounded degree-d perturbation give √n≤λ≤√n+d. Rooted closed walks have first moments 1,0,d,t_v; substituting their Neumann series into the scalar root gives coefficients d/2, d/2+d²/8, (t_v-d²)/2 and a uniform O_d(n^-3/2) residual by f′≥1. Nine standalone graph calculations compared independent numerical methods, but are not relied on for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The source 2026 paper contains the local/global inequality, not the all-regular fixed-edge-budget fan-vs-matching asymptotic. The 2012 coupling resolvent and 2013 exact matching eigenvalue (and general perturbation) are acknowledged as existing. The claimed contribution is the new uniform high-order hub expansion with the first vertex-triangle coefficient and its structural same-budget contrast; no stronger statement covering it was identified in the inspected full texts or indexed searches. General spectral graph folklore remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be certified from web and semantic indexed search; an earlier spectral asymptotic for a vertex joined to a regular layer may be equivalent.
The 2021 walk-based spectral work was available only in excerpt, so no full-document exclusion is claimed.

The 2013 generic strong-coupling asymptotic implies the first two coefficients of the hub case under suitable uniformity; originality is confined to the complete uniform expansion and triangle correction.

value.rationale: Community threshold sets and intercommunity link budgets are natural epidemic network summary statistics. The theorem proves their asymptotic insufficiency even when the complete within-community graphs match, quantifies a divergent spectral vulnerability factor, and isolates the first local motif in a uniform high-order expansion. This is a mathematically motivated structural counterexample rather than a routine numerical plug-in or a new definition.
